item.title: Newsletter: 👎 Lower Fines for Reckless Drivers? / 🚃 Reimagining Regional Rail / 🚶 Sunday: Walk for a Safer Route 13
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #44 · September 23, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

👎 LOWER FINES FOR RECKLESS DRIVERS?

🚃 REIMAGINING REGIONAL RAIL

🚶 SUNDAY: WALK FOR A SAFER ROUTE 13

⏪ A BUSY WEEK RECAPPED

Our transit committee met last Tuesday and they welcomed guests from Transit Forward Philly and SEPTA. We discussed the Transit Access Fund, accessibility audits, and SEPTA's youth outreach and education efforts.

And on Wednesday, we had a great time in Roxborough Pocket Park at our fifth Northwest Philly meetup. We were thrilled to host guests from Roxborough Development Corporation, Transit Forward Philly, Representative Tarik Khan's office, the Bicycle Coalition, and Philly Bike Action.

We closed the week out by showing up to City Council's first session to support Transit Oriented Communities. We're working to expand coverage to additional SEPTA stations--sign here to help make it happen.

🌳 CENTER CITY OPEN STREETS

🗞️ 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

💰🚲 SAVE FEDERAL BIKE FUNDING

DOT Secretary Sean Duffy is asking Congress to end federal funding for bike lanes and even remove existing bike lanes from roads that receive federal funding. Tell your representatives in Congress: Save Our Bike Lanes!

 

✍️ CENTER CITY CONCOURSE SURVEY

Center City District is exploring ways to reimagine the Center City Concourse--respond to their survey to share your feedback!

 

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

📅 EVENTS

Sep 27

Route 13 Advocacy Walk

10:00 AM to 6:00 PM · Hunting Park

Between 2019 and 2023, Route 13 has seen 123 fatal and serious injury crashes--it's time for a change. Advocates, friends and families of victims of traffic violence are walking Route 13 to raise awareness about the need for speed cameras to reduce crashes and saves lives.
Oct 2

Rewriting the Family Home: Three Philadelphia Authors Imagine A Way Out of the Single-Family Housing Trap

4:30 to 6:30 PM · Village of Industry & Art, 320 S Broad St

Three Philadelphia-area writers--Rachel Pastan, Diana Lind, and Samantha Paige Rosen--will discuss the ways current zoning makes finding a way and place to live in the world increasingly and unnecessarily hard. They will share how they have each used research and imagination in their recent books to vividly and engagingly describe the problem and envision alternatives.
Oct 5

PBA Citywide Meeting -- School Streets

6:30 to 7:30 PM · Philadelphia Ethical Society, 1906 Rittenhouse Sq

Join PBA for their next citywide meeting featuring guest speaker Marisa Jones speaking about how she helped bring about Philadelphia's first school street
Oct 8

Life in the Floodable Landscape

12:00 to 1:30 PM · Annenberg Center for the Performing Arts, 3680 Walnut St

Penn Urban Studies is hosting Kian Goh, associate professor of urban planning at the UCLA Luskin School of Public Affairs, for a free lecture on flooding and urban environments.
Oct 14

The Original Transit-Oriented City: Transit-Oriented Communities and Philadelphia’s Next Era

5:30 to 7:00 PM · Village of Industry & Art, 320 S Broad St

Join Design Advocacy Group and representatives from DVRPC, SEPTA, and the Philadelphia City Planning Commission for a discussion on how to leverage the region’s transit network to create and sustain neighborhoods that prioritize people and make walking, biking, and transit convenient, attractive transportation choices.
Oct 17

Making All Stops - Transit Arts Event

1:00 to 3:00 PM · The Rotunda, 4014 Walnut St

Making All Stops is a community storytelling production where SEPTA riders read their own short pieces about their metro memories, their SEPTA stories, their moments of transit and trust, care and connection. To be a part of it, fill out this form.
Oct 29

Pitchfest: Transportation

2:30 to 6:30 PM · Penn Museum, Widener Lecture Hall, 3260 South St

Transportation Initiative at Penn is hosting an event designed to connect transportation-focused public agencies with faculty and staff at the University of Pennsylvania to collaborate on applied research projects. Public agency staff are invited to give low-stakes, two-minute pitches on short-term, high-impact projects that could benefit from external expert support.

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

WHYY / Report: Center City apartment construction boom aids Philadelphia’s long-term housing goals

The Inquirer / A 43-unit apartment building that preserves historic features is proposed in Old City

The Inquirer / A 122-unit duplex development is planned just west of Girard Estates

The Inquirer / A gated community of 140 townhouses is proposed near Packer Park

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

Audacy / SEPTA considers restoring historic Shawmont Station in Roxborough

🚌 TRANSIT

Philly Voice / SEPTA shifts gears in pitch for funding, showing what money could buy instead of doomsday scenarios

NBC10 / SEPTA bus operators put skills to the test in annual ‘Roadeo'

🚲 MOBILITY

The Inquirer / Will a pedestrian death move Philadelphia police to step up traffic enforcement? | Shackamaxon

The Inquirer / Society Hill neighbors are spending $54,000 on a traffic study to examine bike lanes

Billy Penn / The status of the Spring Garden Connector project

💼 JOB OPPORTUNITIES

YIMBY Action / National Organizing Director

Philadelphia Housing Authority / Leasing Coordinator

Esperanza / Housing Counselor - Bilingual

Only One / Chief of Staff

Office of Councilmember Gauthier / Zoning & Community Development Representative

Philadelphia Chinatown Development Corporation / Housing Development Project Manager

Friends of the Wissahickon / Business Manager

Bartram's Garden / Director of Facilities and Safety

Philadelphia Corporation for Aging / Quality Improvement Manager

City of Philadelphia and SDP / Youth Climate Action Microgrants

YIMBY Action / National Organizing Director

Philadelphia Visitor Center Corporation / Chief Financial Officer

Fairmount Ventures / Senior Consultant, Fundraising

City of Philadelphia

  • Chief of Staff - Managing Director's Office
  • Workforce Development Manager - Transportation and Infrastructure

Feet First Philly / Public Space Enhancement Mini-Grant (Deadline 10/3)

SEPTA / Bus Operator / Light Rail Operator, City

PBA / (Grant) Community Action Fund (Deadline 10/2)

DVRPC / Planning Fellowship

Econsult

  • Analyst
  • Senior Analyst

NV5

  • Transportation Engineer

  • Transportation Project Manager

We need your support to sustain Philly's Urbanist Movement — and you get cool perks too.

Join Us as a Member TODAY

Weekly Newsletter #40 · August 26, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🍻 SEPTEMBER MEETUP

Join us on September 15th from 6 to 8pm for a meetup in Roxborough Pocket Park!

🚌 NEW BUS NETWORK ROLLOUT

🔰 LAND VALUE TAX DISCUSSION

🪑 THIS WEEKEND: PEDESTRIANIZED SOUTH STREET

The event will feature live music, food, and a movie.

🎫 CITYNERD LIVE IN PHILLY

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes! And use this tool for a quick form letter to contact your representatives.
